1  ACQUISITION ACT, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED  16.07.2009 PASSED IN LAC.NO.235/2004 ON THE FILE OF THE  ADDITIONAL CIVIL JUDGE (SR DN), JAMKHANDI, SITTING AT  -2-  MFA No. 23268 of 2009 MUDHOL, PARTLY ALLOWING THE REFERENCE PETITION FILED UNDER SECTION 18(2) OF L.A.ACT.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The claimants have preferred this appeal challenging the sufficiency of compensation awarded in LAC.No.235/2004 on the file of the learned Additional Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.), Jamkhandi, sitting at Mudhol (hereinafter referred to as the 'Reference Court') vide judgment and award dated 16.07.2009.
2. The parties are referred to as per their rank before the Reference Court for the sake of convenience.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the claimants claimed compensation for the land bearing Sy.No.49/2 measuring 1 acre situated at Uttur village of Mudhol Taluk, which was acquired under the notification.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer ("The SLAO" for short) awarded compensation of Rs.96,024/- per acre, whereas the Reference Court awarded compensation at Rs.1,80,000/-.
The same is being challenged before this Court by the claimants seeking enhancement.
4. Heard Miss. Ratnamala G.H., learned counsel for the appellants.
Though notice is served on the respondent-SLAO, remained unrepresented.
5. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that Sy.No.49/2 measuring 1 acre owned by the claimants was acquired by the respondent.
The claimants have led evidence before the Reference Court and produced the relevant documents.
Sufficient materials are placed before the Court to show that the sugarcane was being grown in the land in question.
The land was acquired for the purpose of installing the grid as the same was adjacent to main road.
The evidence of PW.1 discloses that Sy.No.49/2 belonging to the claimants was hardly about 2 or 3 kilometers away from Sy.No.47/2 which was converted into non-agricultural land.

Ex.P.12 is produced by the claimants which is the sale deed dated 09.04.2003 where under properties bearing Nos.745 and 746 with plot Nos.11 and 20 measuring 903.84 sq.ft. formed in Sy.No.47/2 was sold for Rs.23,500/-.

Therefore, it is the contention of the claimants that the adjacent land was sold during the notification at Rs.26/-
per Sq.ft. and Sy.No.49/2 which was acquired was also having NA potential, is entitled for enhancement of the compensation.

sentences.text: The Apex Court has highlighted as to which are the aspects that are to be taken into consideration while determining the compensation based on the marked value reflected in most comparable instances.
The proximity of situation and proximity of the time are the two aspects amongst others that are taken into consideration in determining the compensation.

Exs.P.10 to P.12 came into existence in close proximity to the date 1988 AIR 1652 of notification and PW.1 has deposed regarding those documents and he is entitled for enhancement of the compensation.
Accordingly, she prays for allowing the appeal and fix the value of the land acquired at Rs.10/- per sq.ft. in the interest of justice.
7. Inspite of giving sufficient opportunity, the respondent-SLAO has not appeared either in person or by his advocate to address his arguments.
Hence, the argument on the respondent side is taken as nil.

8. Perused the materials on record.
9.

My answer to the above point is in the affirmative for the following:
REASONS 11.
The only contention raised by the learned counsel for the appellants is that Sy.Nos.47/2 and 49/2 are adjacent to one another, they are situated within about 2 or 3 kilometers away.
Sy.No.47/2 was converted into non-agricultural land as per order passed by the Deputy Commissioner dated 26.07.2002.
The said order is produced as per Ex.P.10.

Ex.P.11 is the proceedings of the meeting of Uttur Gram panchayat, taluk Mudhol approving the mutation of the name of Balappa Ramappa together measuring 903.84 sq.ft., formed in the converted land, sold for total consideration of Rs.23,500/- under Ex.P.12, the copy of the sale deed.
The evidence of PW.1 discloses that Sy.Nos.47/2 and 49/2 are adjacent to one another and lying within 2 or 3 kilometers away in the same village.
Admittedly, the land in question belonging to the claimants was acquired for the purpose of installing the grid.
From these materials, it could be concluded that the Sy.No.49/2 belonging to the claimants had non-agricultural potential.
12. When the materials that are placed before the Court disclose that the property which is adjacent to the land which was acquired was sold for Rs.26/- per Sq.Ft.
But the fact remains that Ex.P.12 the Sale deed is subsequent to the issuance of 4(1) notification notifying acquisition of land.
Moreover the value of the land at Rs.26/- per sq.ft. was fixed after conversion and forming of layouts.

13. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that the claimants are not seeking enhancement of compensation at the rate of Rs.26/- per Sq.Ft., but they are seeking compensation at the rate of Shivalingayya vs The Spl. Land Acquisition Officer on 6 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5768797/
3 Rs.10/- per Sq.Ft., and accordingly they have paid the Court fees.

entities.text: Shivalingayya vs The Spl. Land Acquisition Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, even though Ex.P.12, the sale deed came in to existence after issuance of 4(1) notification, the claim of the claimants for fixation of the market value at Rs.10/- per Sq.Ft. is just and reasonable, which can be fixed by this Court.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the just and reasonable compensation at the rate of Rs.10/- as claimed by the claimant could be fixed.
14. In view of the above, the appeal deserves to be allowed.
Hence, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following ORDER 1.
The appeal is allowed with costs.

3. The appellants are entitled to receive compensation in respect of the land bearing Sy.No.49/2 measuring 1 acre situated at Uttur village of Mudhol Taluk is fixed at Rs.10/- per Sq. Ft., with all statutory benefits.
2. The impugned judgment and award dated 16.07.2009 passed in LAC.No.235/2004 by the Reference Court is accordingly modified.
Registry is directed to send back the Trial Court Records along with copy of this judgment.
